_comment: EVERY SATELLITE'S ZONE — a farm you have to BUILD, which is the difference
between one of these and the hub and the reason this file is short.
SHARED BY BOTH SATELLITES rather than copied per island, and that is the
point of the name. They were ratified as the same 24x24 farm, so two
identical files would be one authored thing in two places, drifting the
first time either is edited. A zone is a PATH in content::kIslands, so
sharing one is a registry decision and costs nothing; when a satellite
earns its own shape it gets its own file and the other keeps this.
The hub's zone (worlds/farm.world.json) is a whole steading: a mill, a coop,
a yard, a fence and a lane. Copying that here would have made the satellite
the same farm twice, and duplicated five authored entities that would then
have to be edited in two places forever. What it gets instead is the FENCE
and nothing else: the board's boundary, so 576 plots do not simply stop, and
bare ground inside it.
SO THERE IS NO MILL AND NO FLOCK HERE, deliberately. view::Steading is built
for exactly this - `a missing locator costs that feature and says so` - so
the mill's sound and the birds are absent rather than broken, and the player
buys a mill when they want one. That is also what makes arriving somewhere
feel like arriving: the same 24x24 board the hub has, and nothing on it.
The board itself is NOT authored, here or anywhere: the plot table lives in
the sim's WorldView and view/ mirrors it (H1 plan 3a). This file is what
STANDS on the island, not what grows on it.
name: satellite_farm

entities._comment: The field's boundary, the same baked mesh the hub uses — one entity, 540 triangles, with a gate on +Z. Shared as an ASSET rather than copied as content, which is the distinction: two islands may both have a fence without either owning the other's steading.
